Index.subtitle: Climate Resonances

Index.help-text-2: Click and drag the Marker to move it somewhere else
Index.aboutTextp1: Based on geolocation data chosen by users, the GaiaSenses app generates real-time animation and a soundtrack. Fire spots come from NASA's FIRMS system, from the VIIRS instrument aboard the NOAA-20 satellite. Lightning strikes are derived from the GOES-19 weather satellite, operated by NOAA, whose GLM product is read directly from its public repository. Weather conditions — temperature, humidity, wind, rain, clouds and pressure — come from the Open-Meteo platform, and the name of the chosen location is resolved by OpenWeather. The GaiaSenses app is being developed at CTI Renato Archer, in the Cyber-Physical Systems Division (DISCF/CTI), by an interdisciplinary team of researchers, the GaiaSensers. Animations and soundscapes are driven by these meteorological and climatic data, such as fires, lightning, and precipitation. Information from planetary platforms serves as inputs or parameters for generative algorithms and other creative computational techniques.
Index.aboutTextp2: We adopt the climate as the main instigator for sensory experiences, believing that creative engagement with climate data can activate productive knowledge networks, potentially transformative. Multidirectional flows between artists and scientists, data and instruments, occur in pursuit of creative results that not only disseminate climate phenomena but also generate affective forms, aiming to create an emotional connection with the planet and promote the possibility of transformation.

Index.acknowledgementText: This work wouldn't have been possible without the support of the researchers from CEPAGRI, Dr. Priscila Coltri, Dr. Renata Gonçalves, and Dr. Jurandir Zullo Jr., M.Sc. Bruno Bainy, and Engineer Bruno Veloso. The GaiaSenses project also received support from Prof. Dr. Amílcar Cardoso and Dr. Pedro Martins from the University of Coimbra, Prof. Dr. Jônatas Manzolli (IA-NICS) and Prof. Dr. José Fornari (NICS) from the University of Campinas (UNICAMP), Dr. Josué Ramos from DISCF/CTI Renato Archer, and Ph.D. Anésio Azevedo Costa Neto from IFSP. Students from various departments at UNICAMP have been contributing to the development of GaiaSenses, including Cássio Dezotti, Gabriel Kuae, Tauane Cardoso, and Ru Yi Shen from the Control and Automation Engineering Faculty; Elton do Nascimento, Thiago Lacerda, Isabella Rigue, and Felipe Santana from the Computer Engineering Institute.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.intro: GaiaSenses is an art-science research project that turns the climate data of where you are into audiovisual compositions. To do that it uses some data — this page describes what, why, and for how long.
Privacy.locationP1: When you open the site, the hosting platform (Vercel) estimates your city from your IP address. It is an approximate, city-level location, used only to point the globe and pick a composition matching the weather where you are. We do not store your IP.
Privacy.locationP2: That estimate lives in a cookie named userLocation for 24 hours, unreachable by page scripts (HttpOnly) and sent only over HTTPS. Using the device GPS is optional: it only happens if you tap the location button and allow it in the browser, and the result is not stored by us.
Privacy.corpusP1: When a composition plays, we record: the composition name, the climate values at that moment (temperature, humidity, wind, lightning, fire spots), the time on display, and the coordinates involved — reduced to a cell of roughly 4 km before being written. This record holds no name, account, e-mail or IP address.
Privacy.corpusP2: This data feeds the project's research: understanding how climate shapes the compositions the audience experiences.
Privacy.pushP1: If you subscribe to notifications, we keep the name, e-mail and frequency you choose, together with the browser's technical delivery address. Notifications are delivered by browser push; the e-mail identifies your subscription and lets us contact you about it. The unsubscribe button removes that subscription. Sign-up attempts are rate-limited at the hosting edge, without storing your IP in our database.
Privacy.thirdP1: To draw the map and fetch the weather, the site queries Mapbox (map), Open-Meteo (weather), OpenWeather (place name) and our satellite backend (fire spots and lightning, from public NASA/NOAA data). These services receive the queried coordinates — the point the globe is looking at — never your identity.
Privacy.rightsP1: Under the Brazilian data protection law (LGPD, Law 13,709/2018), you can request access, correction or removal of your data — the notification subscription, for instance — by writing to gaiasenses.cti@gmail.com.
